Subject: Atlas Health — Term amendment & capacity uplift: kickoff and QBR scheduling

Hi Caroline (and Atlas procurement),

Thanks again for the productive QBR last month. As we discussed, Atlas is at the point where a predictable committed path will better support your burst and multi-region needs. I wanted to kick off a short coordination thread to align on:

- proposed term amendment (24-month commitment vs current 12-month)
- committed throughput uplift (proposal below)
- pricing and discount mechanics tied to the uplift and term length
- procurement/redline timeline and DocuSign target
- scheduling a focused QBR to review operational transition and runbook

High-level proposal (for discussion):
- Term: 24 months starting 2028-01-01
- Committed tokens/month: 150M (current paid commitment: 50M)
- Dedicated burst pool: 2x current GPU hours for alerts and clinical peak windows
- Pricing: blended unit price with a volume discount and a one-time onboarding credit (TBD)

Next steps I propose:
1) Atlas confirms stakeholders for contracting (legal/procurement + engineering ops)
2) Redwood provides a redline (attached v3) and throughput rationale workbook
3) Quick 45-minute QBR on week of Nov 1 to finalize runbook and SLAs

Options for QBR slots (PST):
- Tue Nov 2, 10:00–10:45
- Wed Nov 3, 13:00–13:45
- Thu Nov 4, 08:30–09:15

Ben — looping you in to own commercial terms and to surface any early pricing scenarios. Marissa/Vivek — can you prepare an ops checklist and a short draft QBR agenda to attach?

Caroline — if you can confirm preferred QBR slot and the procurement contact, I’ll get the decks and redlines prepared for review.

Thanks,

—
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
email: tessa.morgan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Tessa — thanks for the summary. We’re optimistic about a longer-term commitment if the numbers and operational guarantees are solid. Quick answers:

- Procurement lead: Daniel Park (cc’d) — he’ll own the contract review and can loop legal if needed.
- Ops/Engineering: I’ll bring Katherine and our infra lead to the QBR (they’re out of office next week but available Nov 2 & 3).
- Preferred QBR: Nov 2 10:00 PST works for our team.

A couple of asks before the QBR so we can brief leadership internally:
1) A concise one-pager that explains the throughput uplift math and expected cost delta month-over-month (high level — we don’t need full detail).
2) A clear fallback policy: if we go above the committed throughput, what are the overage rates and emergency burst guarantees?

We’ll aim to have preliminary redlines back within 5 business days after we see your updated commercial doc.

Best,
Caroline
Director, Data Platforms | Atlas Health

Caroline — great, thanks for confirming Nov 2 at 10:00 PST. I’m attaching a short commercial brief and a draft QBR agenda for the meeting. Key notes from my side:

- Pricing scenarios included: (A) 24-month committed with 150M tokens/mo; (B) 18-month phased uplift (100M -> 150M in month 7). Both include a tiered unit price with a 12%–20% discount band depending on commitment and payment terms.
- We can include a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 5% of the first-year committed spend if Atlas signs within 30 days of the redline agreement.
- Overage policy: 1.5x standard unit price for any usage beyond committed tokens; emergency burst pool (pre-approved) guaranteed within 2 hours for operational peaks (subject to pool availability).
- DocuSign flow: we’ll prepare an exhibit for capacity and an amendment template. Expected turnaround from Redwood side: 3 business days for initial exhibit prep after we align on slot.

Marissa — FYI, can you confirm operations runbook owners and whether we have a dedicated SRE on-call for Atlas during their peak windows? Vivek — we’ll want to ensure the dedicated burst pool can be routed regionally for their east-coast failover.
